counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.017675557924424625 to 0.008 (single field change) - finer integration resolves close-approach forces and momentum stays conserved for all 9 steps, confirming violation was due to insufficient time resolution / substep count during the 0-1 close encounter.

explanation: Shrunk scenario has 3 bodies with large masses (17.12, 18.30) and G=4.72 and dt=0.0176. Bodies 0 and 1 undergo close approach: distance ~1.45 at step 9 vs no close pair at step 8. Momentum was exactly conserved through step 8 (total momentum = initial value), but jumps at step 9 by 0.309 (> allowed 0.211), and angular momentum also jumps, indicating integration error in the adaptive leapfrog substepping. Substeps increased from 10 at step 8 to 11 at step 9, insufficient to resolve the steep softened force. Halving dt removes the violation, confirming numerical integration error during close encounter.
vision_note: Frames 6-8 show two bodies clustered at the top in close proximity slowly drawing slightly closer while a third body on the left remains almost stationary. At step 9 the top pair appears marginally closer with a slightly longer velocity trail but there is no abrupt teleport, ejection or discontinuous jump; motion looks smooth and continuous.
